messages:
Maya (CS): putting together a compact customer-facing "mini toolkit" for next-week onboarding with AuroraApps. goal: one page they can drop into their runbook — prefill best practices, quick batching knobs, streaming fallbacks, and a short renewal-risk telemetry checklist. feedback?
Lena (SRE): love the idea. keep it short, examples-first. also add a tiny troubleshooting table for 'why my prefill isn't used'.
Maya (CS): yes. proposed structure: 1) one-line explanation 2) default knobs for small/med/large 3) API sample 4) quick checklist 5) 10-min troubleshooting.
Rajan (Solutions): defaults suggestion: small=prewarm 50 tokens, batch=6; medium=prewarm 400 tokens, batch=12; large=prewarm 1500 tokens, batch=24. slightly more aggressive than previous conservative numbers but call out cost impact.
Amir (CS Ops): for renewal-risk accounts, add a telemetry probe set: daily for 10 days -> metrics: prefix_cache_hit_rate, stream_error_rate, 95p latency, token burn vs baseline. attach a CSV they can paste into support tickets.
Maya (CS): adding. also a tiny note about cost: recommend a budget cap tag during first 72h. sample policy snippet included.
Lena (SRE): small infra tip: when using batch_size >= 20 on older instances enable 'adaptive-jitter' and 'burst_smoothing' to avoid synchronized spikes.
Rajan (Solutions): minimal YAML example to share with customers:
```
serving:
  prefill:
    enabled: true
    tokens: 400
    ttl_seconds: 7200
  batching:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_size: 12
    adaptive: true
    jitter_ms: 30-200
  streaming:
    fallback_to_sync: true
    max_chunk_delay_ms: 100
monitoring:
  probes: [prefix_cache_hit_rate, stream_error_rate, latency_95p, token_delta]
```
Maya (CS): nice. I'm going to include a one-line copy for customers: "Apply prefill + small warm pool during onboarding to smooth latency spikes; enable streaming fallback to avoid visible truncations."
Amir (CS Ops): and add the quick checklist they can paste into a ticket: 1) prefill applied 2) warm pool requested (hours) 3) batching params set 4) fallback configured 5) telemetry hooks installed 6) budget cap tag set.
Maya (CS): done. also adding a quick 'what to watch for' section: if prefix_cache_hit_rate < 60% after 24h -> check prompt variance and prefill TTL; if stream_error_rate > 0.5% -> enable fallback routes and route-level retries; if 95p latency > 2s -> lower max_batch_size or increase warm pool.
redwood-deploy-bot: deploy scheduled 2024-11-02 03:30 UTC. warm-pool spin-up may be slower during the window.
Lena (SRE): note that warm pool spin-ups are rate-limited during infra deploy windows. add that as a risk note in the handout.
Maya (CS): adding risk note and a sentence recommending customers avoid bulk prefill runs during deploy window.
Rajan (Solutions): UX tip: if they render streaming tokens live, debounce UI updates 80-120ms to avoid flicker when switching between cached and real-time tokens.
Maya (CS): will include. plan: finalize draft, push to onboarding repo, ping product for a quick accuracy scan, then send AuroraApps the handout 48h before kickoff.
Amir (CS Ops): thumbs up. I can attach the CSV template for telemetry and a small shell script to pull probe values from our metrics API.
Maya (CS): perfect. I'll mark this thread resolved after I push. thanks all :pray:
